package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a mass campaign (over 140,000 packages) designed to lure users into phishing scams by embedding links to phishing sites in the package description. The packages are auto-generated, use enticing names, and are published at scale to poison the ecosystem and drive traffic to credential-harvesting and referral-reward phishing sites.

execution_context.trigger: package metadata parsing (install-time, search-time, or view-time)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time or when viewing/searching the package, the description field presents enticing text and embedded phishing URLs, luring users to click and visit external phishing sites, leading to credential harvesting or further redirection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding phishing URLs in package metadata is a clear abuse of the package ecosystem for malicious purposes. The text is crafted to entice users with offers of free codes or cheats, a common phishing lure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package descriptions provide information about the software, not links to external phishing or scam sites. Legitimate packages do not attempt to redirect users to unrelated, suspicious domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include links to documentation or project homepages, but not to unrelated, reward-based, or credential-harvesting sites.
key_indicators: Enticing language promising free codes, cheats, or rewards
Multiple external URLs to non-project, non-documentation domains
Use of known phishing or scam domains
No actual software functionality, only SEO/phishing content

attack_chain.action: Automated creation and publication of large numbers of packages with enticing names and phishing links in the description.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users searching for packages encounter the phishing links.

attack_chain.action: User views or installs the package, sees the description, and is lured by the promise of free codes, cheats, or rewards.
User is redirected to a phishing site, which may simulate a reward process and then request sensitive information or redirect to further surveys/referral sites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential harvesting, survey fraud, or referral reward abuse.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing multiple external URLs unrelated to the project
Descriptions with language promising free codes, cheats, followers, or rewards
Mass publication of similarly structured packages with auto-generated names
Descriptions referencing known phishing or scam domains
file_indicators: nuspec files with descriptions containing suspicious URLs
Package names referencing hacks, cheats, free codes, followers, etc.
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as gamecodeclaim.com, tinybit.cc, gamecoins.codes, and other listed IOCs
Redirections to eCommerce sites with suspicious referral IDs (e.g., AliExpress with ?af=... parameter)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package metadata (especially description fields) for external URLs, particularly those matching known phishing or scam domains. Flag packages with enticing language promising free rewards, cheats, or codes. Monitor for mass publication patterns and auto-generated package names. Correlate with known IOC domain lists. Alert on packages with no legitimate code or functionality but containing SEO/phishing content.
